title: Localized comparison source models preserve complex coproducts
statement: Let R,A,B,C be commutative rings in universe u, with R-algebras A,B and an E=A tensor_R B-algebra C. Choose derived categories of R- and B-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let I be a type in u, M_j cochain complexes of A-modules, S another such complex, and s_j:M_j to S a colimiting cofan in the cochain-complex category. For arbitrary universal base-derived tensor cohomology models m_j of M_j and m_S of S [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], and every integer i, let F be termwise extension along A to E to C. There is a C-module isomorphism e from the coproduct of C tensor_E m_j.cohomology(i) to C tensor_E m_S.cohomology(i), such that for every j, coprojection_j followed by e.hom followed by m_S.localizedComparison(i) equals m_j.localizedComparison(i) followed by H^i(F(s_j)). No K-flatness or flatness assumption is made, and the empty family is included.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, derived change of rings, K-flat computation and independence of choices; coproduct specialization of Tag 0DJA(1). Official online versions read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06Y6 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DJA.

proof.text: Choose K-flat R-resolutions of the restricted complexes using the proved ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution, its reduced resolutionFunctor, quasi-isomorphic augmentation, and kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj APIs. Their coproduct has a quasi-isomorphic augmentation by exactness of module sums, and is K-flat because tensor with every acyclic complex commutes with sums. Specialize the fixed-second-factor derived tensor theorem to the complex B concentrated in degree zero. The ordinary one-term tensor is canonically ordinary R-to-B extension; its K-flat computation clause computes the universal derived functor on each P_j and their sum. Compare it with the supplied universal functors by counit uniqueness (pass between the homotopy-quotient counit and its whiskering along the full, object-surjective quotient). Ordinary extension preserves the coproduct of P_j, and the derived direct-sum theorem identifies its localized cofan as colimiting. Naturality of the counit and of the sum augmentation identifies this cofan with the derived images of the given s_j.

Apply derived module homology to the computed coproduct. Compare supplied universal models with the common computation by uniqueness of derived functors and localized model independence. The model-map construction yields E-linear summand maps: derived-functor naturality at multiplication by a in A and cohomologyIso_smul prove compatibility with a tensor 1, while B-linearity supplies 1 tensor b; tensor induction gives E-linearity. The inverse of the B-linear sum comparison commutes with the same actions, hence is E-linear. Thus the E-module cohomologies form a coproduct. Extension from E to C is a left adjoint and preserves this coproduct, giving e.

For every summand map s_j, naturality of the universal counit gives the comparison_eq square. The pure-tensor values ordinaryIso_tmul and ordinaryToLocalized_tmul imply naturality of these fixed maps by tensor generator extensionality. Transpose through extension/restriction adjunction and use localized_eq and adjunction naturality to obtain the claimed localized square. No exactness of E-to-C extension is used. For empty I, the computed complexes and homologies are zero, and the coproduct equations are vacuous.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_localizedComparison_coproduct_source
    (R A B C : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra (A ⊗[R] B) C]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    {I : Type u} (M : I → CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (S : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (s : ∀ j, M j ⟶ S)
    (hs : IsColimit (Cofan.mk S s))
    (m : ∀ j, BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B (M j) C)
    (mS : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B S C) (i : ℤ) :
    let F := (extendScalars.{u, u, u}
      ((algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C).comp (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B)))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)
    ∃ e : (∐ fun j ↦ (extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C)).obj
        ((m j).cohomology i)) ≅
      (extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C)).obj (mS.cohomology i),
      ∀ j, Sigma.ι _ j ≫ e.hom ≫ mS.localizedComparison i =
        (m j).localizedComparison i ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (F.map (s j)) i
